raw_response:
I will keep it close to what I did before, because on 2 mu I cannot gamble. Last year for cotton, I did not chase fancy things. I watched the men around me, and the fields that held more bolls were the ones with enough base fertilizer, water at the right time, and medicine not delayed when insects came. So this year I will still plant cotton on all 2 mu. I will use an improved seed that people around me already planted and saw work, not something strange. For fertilizer, I will not be stingy. Losing yield hurts more than wasting a little fertilizer. On my 2 mu, I will put roughly 1 bag of compound fertilizer as base, then add about half a bag of urea later, and some potash with it, split into two times so the plants do not go hungry when they start growing bolls. With the well, I will water 3 times if the weather is normal: once after establishment if the ground is dry, once around budding and flowering, and once when bolls are filling. If it turns very dry, I will add one more light watering, but for the plan I count 3. I will turn the ground with rotary tillage because my plot is small and that is easier than deep ploughing every year. For pests, I will be watching for aphids, red spider, and bollworms. I will spray about 5 times over the season if needed, because waiting too long always costs more in the end. On a small piece like mine, if management goes smoothly, I will aim for around 320 kg per mu.
